name: FL-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Patronis is a well-funded incumbent with heavy outside support
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~95%
model.rationale: The R+18 district, an incumbent with a massive financial advantage, and markets pricing a Republican win near 95% all point to a safe Republican hold. No polls or expert ratings suggest any reason to move off the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or an unexpectedly strong Democratic fundraising surge could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Florida's 1st District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+18. Incumbent Jimmy Patronis, a former state official who won the seat in a special election, is running for a full term and holds a commanding financial edge: he has raised nearly $3.8 million and benefits from over $2 million in outside support, while Democrat Gay Valimont has raised about $174,000 with modest outside help.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put the Republican's chances around 95%. With the incumbent renominated and no evidence of a competitive environment, the district is expected to remain safely in Republican hands.
